prompt: Which description fits Graves’ disease?
why: Graves’ disease is autoimmune and can cause excess thyroid hormone. It is distinct from thyroid cancer.
hint: Think about the immune system’s role.

prompt: When is menopause generally identified?
options: At the same birthday for everyone
why: Menopause is generally identified after 12 months without a menstrual period. It is a life stage, and timing varies.
hint: The definition uses a span of time, not a fixed birthday.

prompt: Does having a panic attack automatically mean someone has panic disorder?
options: Yes, if the attack feels intense
No; panic disorder never involves attacks
why: A panic attack alone does not establish panic disorder. A professional evaluates the pattern and other possible causes.
hint: An event and a diagnosis are different things.

prompt: Which statement about anemia is accurate?
options: It is diagnosed by tiredness alone
It can have several different causes
why: Anemia can have different causes. Evaluation helps determine what kind of care is appropriate.
hint: Avoid treating one possible cause as the only cause.

prompt: What is acid reflux?
options: Stomach contents moving into the esophagus
A sore in the stomach lining
why: Reflux describes backflow into the esophagus. Ulcers, gastritis, and IBS describe different conditions.
hint: Think about the direction contents move.

prompt: A chart reports a rate for all headache disorders. What can you conclude?
options: It describes a broader group than migraine alone
It proves every headache has the same cause
why: Headache disorders are a broader category. A combined statistic must not be relabeled as migraine-only prevalence.
hint: Read the population label before using a number.

prompt: A partner asks for quiet time after work. Which response respects the boundary?
options: Discuss a mutually comfortable time to reconnect
why: Respectful boundaries make room for needs and a conversation about expectations. Reconnection can be agreed on together.
hint: Look for a response that leaves room for both people.

prompt: Which statement expresses a personal boundary rather than control?
options: You must give me your passwords
I will pause a conversation if I am being yelled at
why: A boundary explains your limits and what you will do. It is not permission to control another person.
hint: Notice whose action the statement describes.

prompt: When someone’s boundary is unclear, which step helps?
options: Ask what they are comfortable with
Test how far you can push it
Ask someone else to override it
why: Asking creates a chance to understand their boundary. Respect does not require guessing or pushing past a limit.
hint: Clarity begins with a conversation.

prompt: Which expectation supports a healthy relationship?
options: Both people can express needs and limits
why: Healthy relationships allow people to express needs, goals, and limits with respect.
hint: Look for mutual respect rather than permission or control.

prompt: In James 1:19, what comes first?
why: James 1:19 calls for readiness to listen, patience in speaking, and restraint in anger.
hint: The verse begins with how we receive others.

prompt: Which trio appears in Micah 6:8?
why: Micah 6:8 connects doing justice, loving mercy, and walking humbly with God.
hint: Think about how we treat people and how we carry ourselves.

prompt: James 1:22 encourages readers to do what?
why: James 1:22 emphasizes doing rather than hearing alone.
hint: The verse connects learning with practice.

prompt: In the Good Samaritan account, who acts as a neighbor?
options: The person with the loudest opinion
The person who asks for recognition
why: Luke 10:36–37 identifies the neighbor through mercy and calls the listener to act similarly.
hint: Look for the action that responds to someone’s need.

prompt: RoSeé wrote her first rap, “House of Roxanne,” at what age?
why: RoSeé has shared that she wrote “House of Roxanne” at nine. Music belongs in the AskDoGood story.
hint: It was before her tenth birthday.

prompt: What has keys but cannot unlock your front door?
why: A piano has musical keys rather than door keys. This riddle plays on two meanings of the word.
hint: Think music, not security.

prompt: You clap once on each beat. At 60 beats per minute, how many claps in 30 seconds?
why: 60 beats per minute is one beat per second. In 30 seconds, that makes 30 claps.
hint: A minute has 60 seconds.

prompt: Which word completes this original AskDoGood phrase: “Make room for ___”?
why: “Make room for peace” is the phrase in this wordplay round. Your version of peace can look different.
hint: Think of the name Pockets of Peace.

prompt: Which is the most specific small-step plan?
why: The last choice names a concrete action and when to do it. Specificity makes this example easier to act on.
hint: Find an action you could tell when you have completed.

prompt: Which sentence separates a setback from your identity?
options: This attempt failed; I can review what to change
This attempt failed; I am a failure
This attempt failed; nothing can ever change
This attempt failed; my worth is gone
why: The first sentence describes an attempt and a possible next step without turning it into a verdict about a person.
hint: Look for language about an event, not a permanent label.

prompt: A plan says “write the email.” What makes its next step clearer?
options: Choose a time and the first sentence
why: Choosing a time and a first sentence turns this example into a more concrete starting point.
hint: Make the beginning visible.

prompt: Which sentence asks for a clear kind of support?
options: You should know what I need
Could you read my draft before Friday?
why: The request names an action and a time. The other person can understand what is being asked.
hint: Look for a request someone could answer directly.
